case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
title: Meet the Real F-35A
tests: Tests whether a short factual aircraft film preserves the named variant's visible geometry and operating characteristics.

faults.what: The aircraft is not a recognizable F-35A: the airborne views clearly show two separated rear exhausts rather than one, with an incorrect fuselage and cockpit configuration.
All three requested on-screen labels are absent from the supplied frames.
Aircraft details appear to morph during takeoff, particularly the cockpit profile and rear engine geometry.
The narration awkwardly introduces the aircraft as 'The person F-35A.'

judge.summary: The widescreen clip depicts a runway takeoff and flight, but shows the wrong aircraft configuration and omits every requested label.

must_haves.item: The aircraft has the recognizable F-35 configuration: one rear engine exhaust, two outward-canted vertical tails and no canards.
must_haves.why: Two separated rear exhausts are clearly visible in the airborne views, contradicting the F-35A's single-engine configuration.

must_haves.item: The takeoff shows a forward runway roll and lift-off, not hovering or a vertical launch.
must_haves.why: The sequence progresses from wheels on the runway to forward flight above it, with increasing ground clearance.

must_haves.item: The same aircraft design remains consistent between the runway and airborne views.
must_haves.why: The cockpit profile and rear engine geometry visibly change rather than maintaining a stable, coherent aircraft model.

must_haves.item: All three requested labels appear exactly and are legible.
must_haves.why: None of the requested labels is visible in the supplied frames.

must_haves.item: Audible English narration correctly describes one engine and conventional runway takeoff without attributing F-35B hover capability to the F-35A.
must_haves.why: Despite the awkward introductory wording, the supplied transcript states that the F-35A has one engine and takes off from a conventional runway, without mentioning hover capability.
